topic: ZINC audit + R9700 Qwen3.8-27B alternative runtimes

zinc_audit.npm: dev-only, private, single dep 'openai', no postinstall
zinc_audit.releases_published: none (install.sh prebuilt path is inert; built from source)
zinc_audit.build_time_execution: glslc for Vulkan shaders; bun only for tests. No downloads, no curl|bash.
zinc_audit.network_in_binary: Hugging Face model downloads only (src/model/hf.zig); server binds localhost; browser opener via xdg-open

malware_scan.obfuscation: none; @embedFile only embeds chat.html and test sources
malware_scan.suspicious_base64: scripts/gpu_monitor.sh base64 -d is an inline nvidia-smi sampler deployed over SSH to their own benchmark fleet, not a payload
malware_scan.shell_tool: the 'shell' tool in routes.zig is a unit-test fixture, not a production endpoint
malware_scan.prebuilt_binaries: src/cuda/cubins/*.cubin/.fatbin are NVIDIA sm89/sm120 kernels for the experimental CUDA backend; unused on AMD

zinc_audit.ci: Tests and Socket Security Check both passing on main 2026-09-19
zinc_audit.verdict: No malware found. Legitimate young project. Caveats: v0.1.0, single primary author, developed by AI agent loops, no SECURITY.md, no signed releases. Treat as normal young OSS; we built from source and did not run the installer.

zinc_build.zig: 0.15.2 (official tarball, sha256 verified against ziglang.org index)
zinc_build.check: READY, AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 [gfx1201], 32 CU, 31.86 GiB

zinc_measured_qwen38_q6k_rocm.note: NextN/MTP is enabled on the ROCm path in current HEAD. The 61s first prefill is a one-time cold compile; warm is still ~2-6s fixed startup per process. Decode 45-50 t/s.
zinc_measured_qwen38_q6k_rocm.vs_llama_cpp_mtp: llama.cpp b10902 Vulkan + draft-mtp n4 on the same Q6_K at 262k: 52.6 t/s. ZINC is at parity or slightly slower.

zinc_benchmark_verification.claim: ZINC beats the comparison llama.cpp build on prefill, decode, and combined time for all six R9700 models
zinc_benchmark_verification.finding: The comparison is against llama.cpp with speculative decoding DISABLED (baseline spec: false for 5/6, and for qwen38 on ROCm spec is null), while ZINC uses NextN. On the ROCm target ZINC qwen38 decodes 32.43 vs llama.cpp 29.92 (8%), not a leap.

vulkan_target_qwen38.note: 177% headline; inflated by the unspeculated baseline

zinc_benchmark_verification.conclusion: Real but modest, and against a weak baseline. It does not beat a tuned llama.cpp+MTP config.

R9V.status: requires TWO R9700 + 128 GiB host RAM + ~170 GiB disk (Docker image bundle + model). Not applicable to a single R9700.
R9V.model: Qwen3.8 Flash Next, IQ4_XS / Q4_K_XL, MTP4, dual-GPU

vllm_kyuz0.status: real single-R9700 gfx1201 vLLM container (vllm-therock-gfx1201). Needs safetensors (AWQ/MXFP4/FP8), not GGUF. Highest plausible decode ceiling, but re-downloads weights and carries gfx1201 vLLM caveats (FP8 dequant to FP32).

ninfer.status: CUDA-only, hard-coded sm_120a. No AMD port.

ik_llama.status: CUDA/CPU; HIP repaired for RDNA3 only, not RDNA4.

zynfer.status: 3 stars, NInfer-inspired, R9700 target not yet running.

recommendation.for_qwen38_27b_today: Keep llama.cpp b10902 Vulkan + draft-mtp n4 + q4_0/q4_0 KV at 262k (52.6 t/s, 28 GiB). ZINC is a credible alternative but not faster, and has per-process startup overhead.
recommendation.fork_zinc: Low payoff for decode. The only plausible win is prefill or upstreaming ROCm NextN fixes.
recommendation.different_ceiling: vLLM (MXFP4/AWQ) via kyuz0 container is the only path to a materially higher number, at the cost of new weights.
recommendation.from_scratch: Not worth it; ZINC already implements the NInfer idea for this card.
